research_question: What do different philosophical and religious traditions say about reincarnation?

indic_traditions.scope: Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, Sikh doctrines of rebirth; karma; atman; jiva; liberation (moksha/nirvana); historical development from Vedic to classical periods
known_sources: Bhagavad Gita - Krishna's teachings on karma and rebirth
indic_traditions.special_instructions: Distinguish between Hindu 'reincarnation' (re-birth) and Buddhist 'rebirth' (no eternal self). Cover Jain vs Buddhist vs Hindu variations.

western_philosophy.scope: Greek pre-Socratic, Platonic, Neoplatonic reincarnation; Western esotericism; 19th-20th century philosophical debates; analytical philosophy of mind on personal identity
western_philosophy.special_instructions: Cover Pythagorean-Orphic roots, Plato's influence on later esotericism, modern analytic philosophy debates (Parfit, Nozick) on personal identity.

ancient_civilizations.scope: Ancient Egyptian afterlife beliefs; Mesopotamian; Gnostic; early Christian; Manichaean; Greco-Egyptian; Zoroastrian; ancient Mediterranean mystery traditions
ancient_civilizations.special_instructions: Distinguish cyclic rebirth (Orphic/Pythagorean) from linear eschatology (Egyptian). Cover Gnostic dualism vs reincarnation.

contemporary_scholarship.scope: Empirical research, NDE studies, philosophical debates on rebirth; Ian Stevenson's methodology; van Lommel Lancet 2001; AWARE study; consciousness studies (Chalmers, Penrose)
known_sources: Ian Stevenson - Twenty Cases Suggestive of Reincarnation
Pim van Lommel - Lancet 2001 NDE study
contemporary_scholarship.special_instructions: Cover empirical methodology debates, critiques (Paul Edwards replication argument), consciousness studies. Clearly separate peer-reviewed from contested claims.
